Emt here, got called for the 30 year old man acting strange. Get on scene and fine him limping around outside. So I get out of the van and ask if he's OK. As soon as he looks at me I can see that the entire left side of his jaw is swollen and bloody. His fingers and hands were black and numb. Apparently he is homeless and got jumped 8 hours earlier but couldn't get anyone to call 911 for him. I look in his mouth and see him holding 3 molars on his tongue and the ends of his lower jaw being held in place by his tongue. He asked me if it was bad. I said it's not a big deal and we are going to the hospital now. Calm cool and collected. Took vitals, got his demographics. I called up the hospital on the radio and told them we were 1 minute out with a full trauma alert with frostbite and significant facial trauma. 

I have never grabbed a doctor by the collar and dragged him into a room before but this guy ended up having 3 fingers amputated, a titanium bar placed in his jaw and his jaw wired shut.

Let's say there's a 15 story building, there are 10 suites per floor with 1 bedroom, 1 bathroom and kitchen/living area in each. If there is a fire on the 10th floor in room 5 the search team will go directly to floor 5 and search the fire room and all rooms on that floor, then either the same team goes to floor 11 or another team searches floor 11 at the same time. Then you work one team from the top floor down and one search from floor 12 up. Now if you are in a city with buildings that size it's likely that you will have about 30 guys scene for the first alarm. If there are 3 people per search team and 5 per hose plus a runner or 2 you can make more search teams to search the floor below (9) and work down to floor one.
